CSIR-UGC NET Earth Sciences: questions by topic, 2012–2025

2915 questions from 20 sittings of the Earth, Atmospheric, Ocean and Planetary Sciences paper (subject code 702). Most papers contain 150 questions; the 2012 paper contains 110 main questions with multipart questions in Part C. The marks per topic are rescaled to what each part actually carries and are directly comparable across years. 2639 of the questions carry the option CSIR or NTA published as correct.

EVIDENCE A session that printed three booklets printed one paper three times in three shuffles — the same questions, reordered — so only booklet A of each session is read here. Reading all three would triple every count and change no weightage.

Trend analysis and forecast for the next paper — year-wise and topic-wise breakdowns, trends, repeated concepts, projected weightage and a preparation plan, each with the arithmetic behind it.

A predicted question paper for CSIR NET 2027 — 150 constructed questions with worked answers, allocated to the projected weightage and grounded in the recurrences documented here. Constructed, not leaked: read the disclaimer on that page first.

EVIDENCE The question text below is machine-extracted from the PDFs CSIR and NTA published. Most are scans of bilingual booklets or of the NTA answer-display screens, so OCR damage survives in the text and 419 of 2915 items could not be classified at all; those are grouped as Unclassified rather than being forced into a topic. The PDFs in this folder remain the authority.

Earth Sciences weightage by topic and year (marks)

INFERENCE Parts B and C only, so each year totals 170 marks. A Part B question is printed at 2 marks and a Part C question at 4, but a candidate answers 35 of the 50 in B and 25 of the 80 in C, so each part is rescaled to the marks it carries — 70 and 100. Where a year held two sittings, its figure is the mean of them: the weightage of a paper, not of a calendar year.
